claims.statement: Directive (EU) 2020/2184 requires domestic-distribution risk analysis and proportionate Legionella measures, with monitoring focus permitted for priority premises.
Polish rules and sanitary guidance require Legionella monitoring in relevant healthcare, public-use and collective-residence hot-water systems and require approved or accredited laboratory testing.

Polish sanitary authorities reported 6695 Legionella tests in 2024 with 1286 poor hot-water-system results (19%), including exceedances at 20% of tested healthcare premises and 15% of tested lodging premises.
ECDC reported a 2024 EU/EEA notification rate of 3.4 Legionnaires' disease cases per 100000, up from 3.2 in 2023.
Laboratory results require system-specific expert interpretation; a negative sample is not a guarantee of absence and analytics cannot replace the building risk assessment or control plan.

Laboratory portals and specialist Legionella platforms already advertise trend analysis, dashboards and portfolio reporting, so differentiation must come from lab-channel deployment and comparable-building outcome benchmarks.

contrary_evidence: Eurofins already offers water-result portals with data intelligence and trend analysis.
LegionellaDossier reports broad installed use and offers historical trends, dashboards and non-compliance management.
Official guidance says samples alone are an imperfect proxy and need competent system-specific interpretation.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with one accredited Polish laboratory as a partner-branded read-only analytics pilot, then sell through lab groups and facility-management contracts.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Planning case, not validated: 100000 samples annually at 40 PLN plus 400 portfolios at 6000 PLN annually is 6.4 million PLN revenue. At 18-22% operating margin and retained founder control, sustained profit could support founder net worth above 5 million PLN; partner conversion, volumes and valuation are unproven.
economics.founder_time: About 3 founder hours daily on analytics and partner operations; accredited labs own sampling and results, while a competent water-safety expert owns interpretations and escalation rules.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Planning range of 60-70% after laboratory share, expert review, secure hosting and support; no public evidence validates the split.
economics.payback: Unknown; require a paid integration pilot whose first-year gross profit covers connector and onboarding cost before building a second lab connector.
economics.pricing: Test 40 PLN per analysed sample plus 6000 PLN annually per multi-site portfolio; both figures are hypotheses and lab/customer willingness is unknown.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Scheduled sampling, remediation retests and recurring risk reviews create repeat events, provided the report changes control decisions and is embedded in the lab portal.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Opt-in, contractually reusable building-system features, interventions and retest outcomes improve comparable-building baselines
fingerprint.customer: Hotels, care facilities, hospitals and multi-site property managers served by accredited laboratories
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner-branded output inside accredited laboratory result portals and facility-management contracts
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Read-only environmental risk analytics sold per sample plus portfolio subscription, with expert escalation
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The property operator pays when a lab-issued trend and control-support report is delivered
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A scheduled Legionella sample, remediation retest or building risk review occurs

founder_fit: Health monitoring and statistical benchmarking fit the founder's interests and data-science skills.
Laboratory partners can own all physical sampling, keeping the initial business part-time and asset-light.
A contracted competent water-safety professional is required; the founder should not personally issue control decisions without qualification.
risks: A report could create false reassurance; it must preserve raw accredited results, uncertainty and urgent escalation.
Laboratories or facility-management suites can bundle trend reporting at no added price.
Sparse, heterogeneous sampling and intervention data may not support valid cross-building comparisons.
Contracts must clearly allocate controller/processor roles and rights to building-level outcomes.

structure.control_point: The traceable interpretation layer between an accredited result, building context and next control action
structure.critical_dependency: Accredited lab integration, competent expert governance, and reusable rights to pseudonymised building and retest outcomes

thesis: Let accredited laboratories attach a read-only, expert-governed building trend and control-support report to each Legionella sampling round, charging per result and portfolio while opt-in retest outcomes improve comparable-building baselines.
title: Legionella Lab Risk Benchmark
uncertainties: Whether accredited laboratories will integrate, share margin and grant outcome-data rights.
Whether property operators will pay beyond the laboratory's existing report.
Minimum sample density and covariates needed for defensible benchmarks.
